resources.string: Draws the Aperture island around your camera, above the status bar. It only learns which app is in the foreground, to hide the island in camera apps. It cannot read what is on your screen, and nothing leaves your phone.
A Pixel-native island around your camera.

Protects the OLED screen: after this time the pill shrinks back around the camera and shows its progress as a thin moving ring, so no fixed shape stays on screen.
Off by default. Messages arrive often, so the island only shows music, timers, deliveries and calls unless you turn this on.

What happened, and what did you expect? (The device report below helps fix it. Remove anything you don\'t want to share.)
Force-stopping Aperture (or a battery tool doing it) switches its accessibility permission off, and Android doesn\'t turn it back on. Open Aperture: the red step shows what to re-enable.
Android shows its own heads-up too. For apps you follow on the island, turn off Settings, Notifications, the app, Pop on screen.
Music is playing but nothing shows.
The island hides while the player app is open. Leave the app. Also check the app is switched on in step 3.
It stopped working after I turned on Advanced Protection.
Android 17 Advanced Protection blocks every accessibility service that isn\'t an accessibility tool, including every island app. Turn Advanced Protection off to use Aperture.
What does Aperture know about me?
Only what is on your notifications and media sessions, while it shows them. It has no internet permission, stores nothing but its settings, and never reads your screen.
Fine-tuning for people who like to tinker. The defaults are chosen to be right for most people.
Only these apps can appear on the island. Suggested apps are on to start with.
Off. Turn on "Aperture island" in Accessibility.

Advanced Protection is on. Android blocks accessibility services that are not accessibility tools, so the island cannot draw until you turn Advanced Protection off. This is a system rule and no island app can work around it.

What the accessibility permission is used for: drawing the island over the status bar, and knowing which app is in front so the island hides in camera apps. Aperture cannot read screen content, has no internet permission, and keeps nothing off your phone.

Black: pure OLED black. Glass: translucent, your wallpaper shows through. Clear: more see-through. Art: the album cover, blurred. Tonal: your theme\'s surface color. The small pill always stays black so it blends with the camera.
